zh-CN.Passkeys improve login security, but sup: Passkeys improve login security, but support teams still need secure account recovery flows that do not recreate password-era weaknesses.
zh-CN.The practical reason this topic is getti: The practical reason this topic is getting attention in 2026 is simple: more users are adopting passwordless sign-in across devices and platforms. For product and support teams rolling out passkeys to customers, the question is no longer whether the trend is interesting. The question is where it changes daily work enough to justify new process, budget, or risk review.
zh-CN.The common failure mode is making recove: The common failure mode is making recovery so easy that attackers target support instead of login. That mistake usually happens when a trend is treated as a feature checklist instead of an operating change. The technology may be new, but the weak point is often ownership, permissions, data quality, recovery, or review.
zh-CN.Before picking a vendor or writing code,: Before picking a vendor or writing code, decide how legitimate users regain access after device loss without exposing accounts. A clear first decision keeps the team from mixing experiments, production systems, sensitive data, and customer promises into one blurry rollout.
zh-CN.Start small: combine device signals, ste: Start small: combine device signals, step-up checks, recovery codes, waiting periods, and support scripts. Keep the first version narrow enough that success and failure are both visible. That makes it easier to compare quality, cost, latency, privacy, and support load before expanding the workflow.
zh-CN.A mature workflow produces a recovery pl: A mature workflow produces a recovery playbook that is secure, explainable, and measurable. It should be easy for someone outside the implementation team to inspect what happened, understand why it happened, and decide whether the result is reliable enough to act on.
zh-CN.Set a review date, a measurable success: Set a review date, a measurable success criterion, and a rollback path before launch. If the passwordless recovery workflow does not improve the actual decision, reduce risk, save time, or create a clearer user experience, keep it in research instead of forcing it into production.
zh-CN.Define the use case for passwordless rec: Define the use case for passwordless recovery before choosing tools.
zh-CN.Name the main risk: making recovery so e: Name the main risk: making recovery so easy that attackers target support instead of login.
zh-CN.Make the first decision explicit: how le: Make the first decision explicit: how legitimate users regain access after device loss without exposing accounts.
